start.title: Return to the Throne
start.text:
Pharaoh sits cold upon his throne.
Aaron stands at your side.

choices.text: Cast down the staff before him
choices.feedback: Exodus 7:9-10 — The Lord commanded Moses and Aaron to cast down Aaron's staff before Pharaoh, and it became a serpent.

hide_consequence.title: Speak the Sign
hide_consequence.text:
He sent you to show His power.
Do not silence the Lord here.

choices.text: Cast down the staff before him

storm_consequence.title: Do Not Walk Away
storm_consequence.text:
Pride will not free your people.
Return and obey.

choices.text: Cast down the staff before him

serpent_sign.title: Magicians Match the Sign
serpent_sign.text:
Their staffs become serpents too.
Yet yours devours theirs whole.

choices.feedback: Exodus 7:14-16 — After the magicians' staffs also became serpents and Aaron's staff swallowed theirs, the Lord told Moses to tell Pharaoh to let His people go.

boast_consequence.title: Not Your Glory
boast_consequence.text:
He alone undid their craft.
Speak only what He gave.

to_the_nile.title: Beside the River
to_the_nile.text:
Pharaoh comes down to the Nile.
The Lord says: strike the water.

choices.text: Wait for him to ask first

choices.feedback: It is a sign, not a plea.

choices.text: Strike the water with the staff
choices.feedback: Exodus 7:19-20 — The Lord commanded Aaron to stretch out his hand with his staff over the waters of Egypt, and they would turn to blood.

wait_consequence.title: Now Is the Hour
wait_consequence.text:
His word does not wait on kings.
Lift the staff and strike.

choices.text: Strike the water with the staff

beg_consequence.title: Not a Plea, a Sign
beg_consequence.text:
He sent judgment, not a prayer.
Do what He commanded.

choices.text: Strike the water with the staff

nile_blood.title: Seven Days of Blood
nile_blood.text:
Fish die. Egypt cannot drink.
Pharaoh's heart will not bend.

choices.feedback: Exodus 8:1-2 — The Lord commanded Moses to tell Pharaoh that if he refused to let the people go, He would plague all his country with frogs.
Speak the Lord's word, not yours.

mock_consequence.title: His Word, Not Mockery
mock_consequence.text:
Pride does not break a king.
Deliver the warning given you.

frogs_plague.title: Frogs Cover the Land
frogs_plague.text:
They fill the houses, ovens, beds.
Pharaoh begs you: "Pray for me."

choices.feedback: Exodus 8:8-12 — Pharaoh asked Moses and Aaron to entreat the Lord to take away the frogs, and Moses cried out to the Lord concerning the frogs.
Mercy is not yours to barter.

refuse_pray_consequence.title: Mercy Is His to Give
refuse_pray_consequence.text:
When a king begs, you carry it.
Pray as you were told.

silver_consequence.title: His Mercy Is Free
silver_consequence.text:
The Lord asks no payment from you.
Do not stain His name with greed.

pharaoh_lies.title: The First Lie
pharaoh_lies.text:
Frogs die. The land stinks of them.
Pharaoh's heart hardens again.

choices.feedback: Exodus 8:16-17 — The Lord commanded Aaron to stretch out his staff and strike the dust of the earth, so that it might become gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.

despair_consequence.title: He Is Not Done
despair_consequence.text:
His power has only begun to speak.
Lift the staff again.

swarms.title: "This Is the Finger of God"
swarms.text:
The magicians bow at last.
But Pharaoh will not yield.

choices.text: Take pity and stop the signs
choices.feedback: Mercy is not yours to grant.
Exodus 8:20-21 — The Lord commanded Moses to tell Pharaoh that if he did not let His people go, He would send swarms of flies upon him, his servants, his people, and into his houses.

boast_again_consequence.title: His Finger, Not Yours
boast_again_consequence.text:
It is the Lord they confess.
Do not steal what is His.

pity_consequence.title: Not Yours to Stop
pity_consequence.text:
Pharaoh's pride must be broken.
Deliver each word, in order.

livestock_die.title: Cattle Fall in the Field
livestock_die.text:
All Egypt's herds lie dead in dust.
Israel's flocks graze unharmed.

choices.feedback: Exodus 9:8-10 — The Lord commanded Moses and Aaron to take handfuls of ashes from a furnace, and Moses was to throw them toward the heavens in the sight of Pharaoh.

hide_wrath_consequence.title: Do Not Hide
hide_wrath_consequence.text:
He goes before you into the court.
Take the soot and obey.

boils_plague.title: Boils on Every Man
boils_plague.text:
Even the magicians cannot stand.
Still Pharaoh's heart is iron.

choices.text: Curse the king to his face
Warn of hail and fire from sky
choices.feedback: Exodus 9:18 — Moses was to warn Pharaoh that the Lord would send a very heavy hail, such as had not been in Egypt since its foundation.
There is no road back now.

curse_consequence.title: His Word, Not Yours
curse_consequence.text:
Judgment belongs to the Lord.
Deliver the next warning given.

choices.text: Warn of hail and fire from sky

give_up_consequence.title: There Is No Going Back
give_up_consequence.text:
He has set you on this road.
Walk it to the end.

choices.text: Warn of hail and fire from sky

hail_fire.title: Fire Walks With the Hail
hail_fire.text:
Crops, beasts, and trees are shattered.
Pharaoh cries: "I have sinned."

choices.feedback: He will lie again. Be ready.
Exodus 9:33 — Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh and spread out his hands to the Lord, and the thunder and hail ceased, and the rain no longer poured on the earth.

trust_consequence.title: Pray, but Know His Heart
trust_consequence.text:
Mercy still answers, even here.
Pray, and watch what he does.

locusts_warning.title: Locusts Strip the Land
locusts_warning.text:
What hail left, the locusts eat.
Pharaoh's own court pleads with him.

choices.feedback: Exodus 10:10-11 — Moses refused Pharaoh's offer to let only the men go, stating that all the people, young and old, with their flocks and herds, must go to hold a feast to the Lord.

choices.text: Accept his offer to free some

side_servants_consequence.title: To the King Alone
side_servants_consequence.text:
Speak the Lord's word to Pharaoh.
Let his servants hear it through him.

accept_consequence.title: Not One Will Stay
accept_consequence.text:
All the people. All their flocks.
That was the Lord's word.

darkness.title: Three Days of Darkness
darkness.text:
No man rises. No fire is seen.
In Goshen, lamps still burn warm.

choices.text: Steal from Egypt in the dark
choices.feedback: He will give them favor in time.
Exodus 10:23 — The children of Israel had light in their dwellings during the three days of darkness.

steal_consequence.title: He Will Provide
steal_consequence.text:
What is given is better than stolen.
Wait for His hand to act.

final_threat.title: "Never See My Face Again"
final_threat.text:
Pharaoh banishes you in fury.
One plague remains, the worst of all.

choices.feedback: His heart is set in stone.

choices.text: Warn of the firstborn at midnight
choices.feedback: Exodus 11:4-5 — Moses declared to Pharaoh that about midnight the Lord would go out into the midst of Egypt, and all the firstborn in the land of Egypt would die.

beg_again_consequence.title: Speak the Last Word
beg_again_consequence.text:
He will not hear pleas now.
Deliver the final warning.

choices.text: Warn of the firstborn at midnight

victory_consequence.title: Not Yet
victory_consequence.text:
The deepest hour is still to come.
Deliver the warning given.

choices.text: Warn of the firstborn at midnight

ending.title: Toward the Night
ending.text:
Egypt is broken. Israel waits.
The last and longest night draws near.
